A Memorable Experience on the Saigon River - Just Be Careful with the Water!
Oct 2026 • Friends
We visited The Deck last Sunday with a group of 19 people, so organising a reservation for such a large group was no small thing. Overall, we had a fantastic and memorable experience!

The atmosphere is absolutely incredible. The beautiful lighting, stunning location right on the Saigon River and relaxed, Ibiza-style vibe, complete with DJ and decks, make this such a special place. It has a wonderful chilled-out feel while still being stylish and lively. Definitely somewhere you go as much for the ambience as the food.

And the food was exceptional! We all ordered different dishes, and every single person was impressed. Everything we tried was absolutely delicious, which is particularly impressive with such a large group.

There were just a couple of things that could have been better. One of our starters never arrived, and the timing of the food coming out was quite inconsistent. Some people had finished their meals before others had even received theirs, which made it a little difficult for the group to enjoy the meal together.

The other thing to be aware of is the table water. We were charged around £15 per family of three or four for water that was repeatedly topped up without being asked. Most of us had only one or two glasses, so this felt very expensive, especially as the charge was more than some of the main courses. It would have been much better to have been clearly informed of the cost and asked whether we wanted the water replenished.

Despite these issues, we absolutely loved our visit. The setting, atmosphere and quality of the food made it a truly memorable experience, and we would happily return. My advice to anyone visiting is to enjoy everything The Deck has to offer, but make sure you clarify the water charges before you start!

Overall, a beautiful venue with incredible food and a fantastic vibe. Definitely worth a visit!

Magical evening with excellent service and refined cuisine
May 2026 • Couples
What a surprising and atmospheric place in Ho Chi Minh City. Upon arrival we were immediately welcomed by torches, candlelight and pleasant music, which together with the many atmospheric lights created an almost magical atmosphere.
The staff were exceptionally friendly, spoke excellent English and took the advisory role around both the dishes and the wine list very seriously. The menu is extensive and offers a lot of choice, both in terms of culinary and wines.
The dishes were tasteful, beautifully presented and served perfectly at temperature. All in all an excellent experience and absolutely recommended for anyone looking for a special night out.

Extremely bad experience
Nov 2023 • Friends
Been there many times, but this time it was really, really bad.
Receptionist, captain: Too bad there's nothing else to say.
Luckily, two staff members saved me at the end.

Bad right from the step of confirming the customer's table reservation. (I booked an outdoor table, right on the riverbank) (right at this step, the restaurant did not confirm or discuss the "rules" for booking a table)

- First: It was raining heavily, we got wet when we went in. My girl friend went first, behind her there was another girl, but the 2 staff members only took care of covering the other girl with an umbrella, letting her go. I have to hide and dodge to get in. It's two employees covering the same girl.

- Next:
 Because it was raining heavily on the day I went, I arrived 30 minutes late, but there was no call from the restaurant, no text message confirming whether I was coming or not. When I arrived, the receptionist said, "Because you're late, our table has been cancelled." Actually, I don't know if the restaurant keeps the table for 15 minutes or 30 minutes or if the order must arrive on time??

- By the time the restaurant told us to sit at a table in the corner, the staff was too crowded. We saw customers with wet heads and necks but couldn't prepare a single sheet of tissue for the customers. When we asked, the staff gave us the menu. First, bring out the tissue paper. (I'm a wet person but still have to give the menu first??)

- The most annoying part is when you bring up "Restaurant Rules" to talk to me. I said above that I set the table outside on the riverbank, but because it was raining that day, according to regulations, we will move our table inside. But from the beginning, I never discussed with me in advance about "If the table is set outside and it rains, the restaurant will move inside, to the corner." When we wanted to change to a guest table, it said "The tables are full". But when I finished eating and returned, those tables still had no customers :)

Will never come back and will never recommend to friends or partners.

It was difficult to get someone to take our orders and once this was done, the drinks took 20 minutes to arrive...and our party had 3 kids so they only had to make 4 cocktails. We had to keep asking if our drinks were finished. However, we ignored it as it was a special occasion and we didn't want to make a scene. 

To be fair to the Deck, the food is good. We all enjoyed our food once it arrived. Now, back to the service.

Our table was the ONLY table in the indoor section. Yet, it was very difficult to get service to take or orders or drinks or even to get someone to refill our water glass (with the large bottle of water we bought). Still we said nothing as it was a special occasion. Finally, we ordered desert. Only 4 deserts. The ice cream was brought out and left at the waiter stand. The desert was left there for about 5 minutes until we asked if this was our food (of course it was as we were the only table in the indoor section). They had to take the ice cream back inside since it already melted. Finally, we went to complain. Enough was enough. Then desert was brought out. But that's not all. We ordered mangoes and was given spoons. Have you tried to eat long cut pieces of mangoes with spoons? 

The chef and the manager finally came over and apologized. Honestly, it takes a complaint for them to notice that one of their big tables were having poor service? Where is the management of this place? Where is the training of the staff? I have lived in Vietnam for 22 years and my experience at other restaurants in this price range is much more refined. Other restaurants have people coming by asking if everything is ok, pouring water, etc. From cocktails to dinner service, truly abysmal. Oh...we were given desert free...Even after explaining to the GM the entire evening fiasco, we were given free desert... And free desert just reinforce the fact that the management thinks the only problem was at the end of the meal. 

I would have given the restaurant a horrible rating except the food was decent. But it's not worth the torture to sit through this for decent food. There are plenty of other restaurants in HCMC.

Maybe just a bad day
Feb 2017 • Couples
I visited The Deck with my girlfriend for dinner, we had:

- the marinated tuna rolls and the spicy chicken salad as starters
- the parrot fish and Irish mussels with french fries as main course

Unfortunately the food did not meet our expectations:

1. The tuna rolls tasted rather plain, also the mouthpieces are way too big. The presentation was trying to be some sort of sushi maki but failed totally as salad, the outer layer and the tuna did not blend at all because the tuna was much too dry and there was no marinade inside. So it was dry tuna, dry lettuce and dry rice paper in a too big roll which got its taste only from the accompanying soy sauce.

2. The chicken salad is far from being a salad in the original sense. You get three circle-shaped tacco-style layers of oily crisp with salty chicken pieces and some tiny vegetable slices and lots of red onions in between. It tries to look fancy but all together just tastes like salty raw onions with plain taccos at a fast food restaurant.

3. The parrot fish was totally overcooked and dry. The fish was cooked too long at the wrong temperature. Either you steam fish or you fry the skin part and then cook it slowly on low temperature so it does not lose moistness inside. This piece was just dry - and delivered lukewarm. The accompanying green bean salad was ok but nothing to remember. The small sauce ball was slipped into the beans while carrying it from the kitchen to our table. This ruined the presentation but the waiter did not care to reposition the items on the plate.

4. The mussles were fresh and tasting good but lukewarm. The french fries were not fried but cooked in oil at too low temperature. They were not golden-brown or crisp but just light yellow and sludgy which shows that the oil was way too cold. Also there was no salt on the fries. The overbaked pieces of baguette which represented small and dry bricks were a joke.

5. All food which was supposed to be served hot was just lukewarm. 

6. The leftovers and dirty plates are stored on a small table within the dining area. When I am not eating at a street food stall I do prefer not to have dirty plates and leftovers and waiters rattling with them close to me. Especially when the waiters are just storing them there for a long time and just leaving them there because obviously no one wants to carry them back to the kitchen.

7. I like spending good money for good food, but there are these small things that make me feel blatantly ripped off. You can order the cheaper La Vie mineral water just in units of 1500ml. If you want less mineral water you have to order a small bottle of Evian which is then more expensive then the La Vie. Come on guys, is it really necessary to make some bucks this way? I know ultra-luxury top 50 fusion restaurants in Bangkok serving free flow high-quality mineral water with fresh mint the whole evening. Do not get me wrong: I am not bragging about one Dollar - it is just the way you present it.

My overall impression: The Deck tries to deliver fancy fusion-style food for the posher Thao Dien clientele but puts more effort into a stylish location and fancy-sounding dishes than in the final delivery. The used raw materials were all high quality but there is a massive lack of craftsmanship. This may work for people who do not really know good food and just visit the place to show off but for anyone preferring the culinary experience over the show off it is a clear disappointment.

2 points.

We booked a table before leaving the UK as it sounded a reasonably upmarket and "our kind of place" location for one of our two nights in HCM, although having read TP reviews just before getting our taxi we became apprehensive (everyone seems unnecessarily hard on the place?). 

But we were impressed! The location is perfect (we resisted the speed boat arrival option as $100 EACH way seemed steep, preferring the £6 taxi) and were given a romantic deck table for our 8.30pm dinner reservation. We started with a beer and a delicious passion fruit type Margarita cocktail, having received prompt but polite and respectful service, plus a handy torch to read the dinner menu .... A good choice of dishes and we were very pleased with prawn and chilli tempura and soft shell crab starters, truly delicious. This food exceeded our expectations, delicious!

Wine menu was great and we selected a lovely Loire Sauvignon for around £28 (come on people, these prices are very reasonable compared to UK) and was poured by waiters exactly when needed and kept chilled in nearby ice bucket. I opted for fillet steak in teriyaki sauce, with asparagus and French fries, and husband for rib eye, both cooked to perfection. 

We were too full for dessert but were served a great cappuccino and an Irish coffee to round off dinner, and the waiters continued to be attentive yet respectful, taking our photo against the charming waterfront backdrop before we left and calling a taxi for us which arrived promptly (and was reasonably priced to take us back to our hotel). 

This was a great evening, an absolutely delicious dinner, and lovely staff. If you happy to pay UK prices for a romantic evening go there!

Multi-faceted Fusion Dining Experience
Jan 2016 • Friends
At the end of our two week tour of Vietnam my husband and our two travel companions would agree that we had already eaten extremely well and experienced the freshest ingredients and the rich exotic flavors that makes Vietnamese cuisine so wonderful. On the evening that we returned to Ho Chi Minh City, my husband who was born in Saigon, suggested we find a good restaurant with a view of the Saigon River. With the help of our concierge at the Caravelle Saigon Hotel we were able to get a table The Deck Saigon. The twenty minute taxi ride from the center of the city to District 2 added as much to our evening as the experience of eating at what I feel is one of the best restaurants in Saigon. District 2 a few years ago was known for being one of the poorest areas of the city. The result of foreign investment and government development its become a modern, urban area. Saigon past and future seem to meet on the ride to the restaurant. Modern city roads provide a view of an elevated urban train system under construction, a sky dotted with large high-rise housing, and centers offering luxury brand shopping. As we approach the restaurant down a narrow residential street we are greeted by the hostess and led through a softly light courtyard, past the the bar and into the dining room which looks directly onto the river. The sophisticated design of the restaurant is magically balanced by the serenity and quietness of the river. We seemed to be transported to another place and time as we watched tug boats push small cargo ships up the river. Equally magical was our meal from the flavorful Foie Gras Dumpling, the tender Sesame Duck Breast and delicate and moist Emperor Fish with Jasmine rice and Chayote squash (Su Su), and the Banana Parfait dessert. Each course was a perfect marriage of Vietnamese flavors and classic European cooking methods. The entire evening over-delivered on our expectations of fine dining at it's best. We will long remember our last night in Vietnam: the old and the new, glamorous urban sophistication next to working-class river, and the modern interpretation of "east meets west" cuisine.

Beautiful view, awesome ambience, great service, but terrible food
Aug 2015 • Family
I'm a little jittery about writing this review since all the reviews so far were raving.

Absolutely agree with everyone on the view, ambience and service. Even the house pour bordeaux was one of the best I had in a while.

But the food, was the worst experience in recent memories. Portions were big but not really a plus point for small eaters like us. We ordered marinated tuna fresh spring rolls, fresh oysters, grilled chicken skewers, black cod, lamb rack and grilled rib eye. (Wish I had photographic memory I can't remember the exact name of each dish). 

But let's start with the positive. The only saving grace was the sesame crackers accompanied with a pate-like mayo-something dip and a sambal belachan dip. Sesame crackers were faultless. The mayo dip was yummy. And nothing can really go wrong with sambal belachan.

For the rest of the food:
1. I love Vietnamese fresh spring rolls - the way the fish or prawn interacts nicely with the herbs and vegetables around it. But their marinated tuna spring roll left a bad clashing taste in my mouth. To be fair, my husband liked it and thought I was weird for hating it.

2. Fresh oysters that didn't really taste that fresh. It had a light mushy texture that lacks that fine taste of the sea. I decided to just stop at one.

3. Grilled chicken skewers were unmemorable and dry. It might have had an interesting twist of lime on it. But I can't remember much.

4. Black cod was generally tender but the skin was over-seasoned with salt. 

5. Lamb rack had was coated with an interesting seasoning consisting of wasabi and maybe pistachio. Accompanying sauce also had a tinge of wasabi. But the lamb rack was tough. Tough to cut, tough to chew on and simply unenjoyable. The four of us could only eat two of the four racks. 

6. We ordered the ribeye cooked to medium. (We had old folks and didn't order it medium-rare as usual.) It was dry, tough and tasteless. And too salty when dipped into the sauce. 

The whole meal came up to 3.7million dong, including two house pours, a glass of cola and a bottle of still water. It was extremely not worthwhile and left me pissy the whole night about my wasted money, my tortured tastebuds and unsatisfied tummy.

It's a stupid idea and doesn't work.

Also, the only carbohydrate side dish on the menu now is jasmine rice, no fries, no mash - nothing. Great if you are on a health kick - but I don't go out for a big fat steak to be healthy! What a crazy choice to reduce the menu options so much.

Also, on this occasion I waited between 5-10 minutes after I had made my choice and put the menu on the table for a waiter to appear long enough for me to catch his attention, to place my order. Sadly this was echoed with the desert menu and the bill. On all three occasions when the wait staff should have been keeping an eye out for customers giving them the nod, there was an unacceptable wait followed by the need to actually shout out the customary "em oi" as staff drifted by our table doing their best to ignore us. 

Not only that, when asking for the desert menu, the waitress (who I think mustve been management level due to her different uniform) curtly acknowledged my request then gestured at another member of staff to deal with it. Said other member of staff didnt understand and there was a further 5 minute wait before someone finally showed enough interest to help us.

After our starters were over, the waiter cleared the serving dishes but left our used plates and cutlery. Par for the course, the way the evening was going. So we put our plates and cutlery onto the adjoining empty table, thinking that they would get the message and replace them with fresh ones when they delivered the mains. No such luck, we had to ask, initially they replaced the plates and then we had to ask again for fresh cutlery. 

Overall the menu changes are disappointing, the choices of sides lacking, the beef on hot stones idea, stupid and the staff inattentive and more concerned with having a laugh with their colleagues rather than keeping an eye on the tables.

This is one of the most expensive places to eat in Saigon, at (by my estimate) an average of 70 USD per head for a 3 course meal and at that price it warrants a much improved experience all round.

There used to be two places in town for a great steak, The Deck and El Gaucho, now there is only one.

Absolutely fantastic
May 2014 • Couples
I can't recommend The Deck highly enough. 

First, the setting is gorgeous. Inside and outside tables have views of the river (if they're not directly adjacent to it!) and the elegantly-appointed interior. We stayed for hours to watch the sunset before our plane flight, and were unexpectedly rewarded with romantic and carefully-lit surroundings. It's apparent that a great deal of attention and taste went into every corner of the space, Something I particularly enjoyed -- a blank white wall on the entrance-side doubles as a screen for silent clips of black-tie events in old movies. It's hard to explain how well this works -- you have to see it. My girlfriend and I could have been served food from Denny's in this restaurant and still felt like royalty.

Conversely, though, I could have been stripped of all my senses except scent and taste, and still felt like royalty. The quality, creativity, selection, and presentation of the food at The Deck were incredible. I don't feel like I really have the vocabulary to express this fully, but suffice to say that this restaurant would mentioned alongside the best restaurants in most, if not all, major American cities. We were there for drinks, but got a wide selection of their dishes -- oysters with a piquant salsa, a young mozzarella appetizer, prawn spring rolls that are easily the best I've had, and several others. The drinks themselves were similarly inventive and delicious. Highlights were a lemongrass-ginger martini, a spicy martini whose name and ingredients escape me, and some kind of orangey, citrusy mix that we couldn't get enough of.

Also, for what it's worth -- my girlfriend is notoriously picky, but that didn't hold her back from loving everything she tried. This is extremely rare.

One thing people might not be expecting is the price. Travelers in Vietnam get used to $1 banh mi and $2 bowls of pho, so it's surprising to end up somewhere with back-home prices -- we were surprised and honestly our traveler's skepticism was aroused. ("Is this overpriced w.r.t. the rest of the country because they're expecting tourists not to realize the expense?") But by the time we had ordered one drink and one appetizer we realized that we were still getting one hell of a deal. This kind of restaurant, food, and service would cost three times more in the states, and it would deserve to, and I would still happily go there on special occasions. I'm sorry I won't get to -- The Deck was one of the top highlights of our extensive tour of the country.

Finally, before I close this out, I have to mention the manager, Geoffrey. He stopped by our table to chat, gave us several recommendations for food and drinks, and generally went above and beyond for us. If you ever end up reading this, Geoffrey -- thank you so much! We will never forget The Deck.

Raiders of the lost Deck
Mar 2014 • Couples
HCMC restaurants had left us underwhelmed. So when I researched The Deck, with its alluring website and gushing reviews, I knew I was onto a good thing.

DIRECTIONS:
It's a 30-minute cab ride from the centre of District One: the Hotel Concierge prepped the taxi driver as to the precise location of the restaurant; and, bless him, he did end up in the very near vicinity before throwing his hands up in defeat.
What ensued was a comical scenario whereby he relied upon ME to guide him ! 
Now I'd never been there before: he spoke no English, I spoke no Vietnamese; and yet (purely by instinct and luck) I got us there !
I knew it was on the river, obviously.

DINING:
Once inside the grounds our senses were tingling; ambient lighting and cool, sultry music, draws you into the gorgeous restaurant.
We'd pre-booked to bag a table by the river: this proved sensible as it was the only one left unoccupied.
Our servers were well-rehearsed and alert: wine glasses were topped up without intrusion and someone always appeared when needed. 
The food was inventive and dee-lish: 
There was only one misfire: my wife ordered the seared tuna and sat back in anticipation of a Japanese-style wedge of tuna, with a purple blush of inner flesh.
Unfortunately, what arrived was more reminiscent of something from our local supermarket, uniformly cooked all the way through: it was actually the colour of used chewing gum.
Of course we could have afforded them the opportunity to put this right, but a strip of tuna (this slim) could never achieve greatness. So we continued without fuss.

Anthony Bourdain would think us cissies for coming all the way to Vietnam and eating at such a smooth restaurant, but we thoroughly enjoyed the evening.
I doubt there are many better venues in the HCMC area: the service was slick, the setting was hypnotic and serene.

PRICING:
Some of the previous reviewers may lead you to imagine this is a wallet-emptying experience:
in contrast, we believe it offers unbelievable value-for-money, when compared with a similar standard back home.
If it weren't for the tuna resembling an insole, I would easily have given it a solid 5/5.

SUMMARY:
Resistance is futile; do yourselves a huge favour and go: they can even send a speedboat to collect you from a jetty near your Hotel (which might be a good idea if your cabbie gets disorientated once he's left District One).
If you do get lost in a taxi, use your phone to call the restaurant (they can direct the driver) otherwise, try Google Earth.

This restaurant is located in District 2, Tao Den, just outside of central Ho Chi Minh City about a $10.00 USD/200,000 Vietnam Dong taxi fare to it's location. It is located along the Sai Gon/Bach Dong River not very scenic river as you can see from the picture posted. It's better to go in the evening at sunset to take advantage of the HAPPY HOUR drinks half priced also the atmospheric ambiance is more rich because you don't have the unscenic river distracting your attention. Compared to other restaurants in it's class, I think this restaurant is slightly over rated and very over priced to value. There are other restaurants (The Blu Bar and Grill) on the river that offer better food for better prices slightly different atmosphere not fine dining. 

For the prices at this restaurant including taxi fare and distance, you might consider eating in the central city. I would recommend an all you can eat bufffet at one of the larger 5 star hotels which would cost about $30.00-40.00 USD a person all you can drink wine included with the meal. Hotels like: Marriot Renniassance, Legend, Caravelle, and Duxton just to name a few. If you want a new and different but costly eating experience, I recommend The Deck.

No better place to enjoy the river
Mar 2013 • Solo
In the years since the Deck first opened it has inevitably risen to the top of the list of must-visit restaurants in Saigon, and for good reason: there is no better place to enjoy the passage of time as demarcated by the sleepy flowing Saigon River.

The food is of a consistent and good quality, combining some Vietnamese with continental and fusion influences. While some may say the menu is confused, it all seems to work: good ingredients, and attention paid to each dish by the chef, rather than offering anything that seems 'de rigeur'. In particular the Phu Quoc prawns, calamari, ostrich steak and caramelized salmon deserve special mention.

While it is open for lunch also, it is the cocktail hour and dinner time that capture the ideal opportunities to let the location shine. Twilight at the Deck is magical. As the heat of the day dissipates, the cool breeze comes through, allowing one to silently enjoy the river as it moves some barges and much floating vegetation along the curves of water. 

No restaurant is perfect, and the Deck has room to improve in certain areas. The wine list has remained largely unchanged through the years, with pricing that discourages consumption. This need not be the case. In a handful of visits the by-the-glass pour came to the table with questionable quality, though in such cases the staff were helpful to quickly replace the beverage. 

Another gripe is not really the fault of the restaurant, but its success has changed the nature of a visit from what used to be a chance for some tranquility to more frequently one where the restaurant is packed to the brim with busloads of tourists. Good business for the restaurant, but certainly a reduced experience for the customer.

For a visitor to Saigon, a visit to the Deck allows an opportunity to experience and see another side of the city...a bit of an urban oasis. This should keep its popular standing for some time to come.

Yes, you need a torch to read the menu but many restaurants do that now, even when your sitting inside. The Deck = The Saigon Sensation
Aug 2012 • Friends
The Deck is in a unique spot on the bank of the Saigon River. This art deco restaurant envelopes you with a tranquil atmosphere, the world music brings a real joining of cultures, not to mention the food - a brilliant and vibrant menu; Vietnamese fusion, fresh as you can get seafood and of course a succulent steak - and for the adventurous you can even try Ostrich!
A service with a smile - the staff at The Deck are not only at your beck and call, they do it with a smile. They seem to really care about the customer - they want them to enjoy their time at The Deck and are willing to accommodate your needs! 
Even getting to The Deck provides an adventure - you can take a small speed boat from the city to The Deck - which I highly recommend - it's the perfect way to see the city in lights! Or for the less adventurous you can take a taxi - you know the form of transport that never differs no matter where you are in the world - if you like familiarity then this option is for you!
What I really loved about The Deck is: The staff, the location and the food – it ticks all the boxes!
The Deck also run TOURS to The Chu Chi Tunnels and to exceed other tour companies, The Deck run this trip by speed boat – so in order to diminish boredom this adrenalin filling ride lets you see all the sights of the river and reduces travelling time.
